docs.title: Prompt audit and final master prompt
docs.body:
## What the original request gets right
It identifies a worthwhile setting, a preventable-harm objective, possible materials, three adoption audiences, and the need to proceed sequentially. The attached response correctly separates fall prevention from impact mitigation and proposes a material-neutral approach.
## Changes applied
| Original gap | Revision | Where resolved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Childproof promise | Use Child-Safer Spaces; promise a process, not zero injuries | 02, 23 |
| Foam as default | Compare source removal, operations, design and commercial cushioning | 04, 08 |
| Broad appeal assumed | Treat appeal as hypotheses and test with adults | 05, 24 |
| Government requirements unspecified | Distinguish law, contract, program rule and proposed incentive | 06, 07, 20 |
| No implementation owners | Name accountable roles and acceptance evidence | 03, 10 |
| No failure pathway | Add stop, removal, incident and restart procedures | 12, 14 |
| No cost/evidence standard | Add whole-life scenarios, controlled pilot and uncertainty | 15–17 |
| No product or procurement assurance | Add performance schedule, dossier and supplier terms | 08, 09, 21 |
| No usable operating system | Offline workspace, editable documents, CSV registers, backup and print | index.html, registers |
| No privacy/change control | Separate sensitive records; version and verify changes | 18, 26 |
## Final master prompt
Develop Child-Safer Spaces, a performance-based, material-neutral program to reduce slips, trips, falls and fixture-impact injuries in businesses children frequent, with access and safety for all customers and workers. Use the U.S. and Canada as initial frameworks, leaving explicit site-specific jurisdiction gates. Treat Walmart only as an example; imply no partnership.
Complete the work sequentially: define scope and stakeholder hypotheses; critically assess evidence and uncertainty; map laws, authorities and candidate standards; compare interventions; specify procurement and testing; design a bounded pilot and economic model; assign governance and maintenance; prepare adoption materials; and deliver an operational HTML bundle.
Provide revised prompts, the substantive solution, stakeholder briefs, a charter, responsibility matrix, authority inquiry, supplier request, technical acceptance schedule, commissioning and daily procedures, training, incident and withdrawal processes, evaluation protocol, data dictionary, financial scenarios, privacy plan, government proposal, insurer questionnaire, landlord and contractor agreement outline, public messaging, adult feedback instrument, scale decision, and reusable registers.
Separate verified facts from recommendations, illustrative figures and unresolved decisions. Cite primary sources, identify their applicability, and never imply foam, playground testing, or an absence of incidents proves retail safety. Do not invent approvals, efficacy, insurance savings, partners or funding. Require accessibility, hygiene, fire, durability, attachment and wheeled-load review of the actual installed system.
Deliver a self-contained offline HTML workspace with role navigation, search, editable templates, export/import of non-sensitive planning work, sequential gate tracking, print-ready handbook, CSV registers, source register and packaged source. Make it possible to begin planning, hazard correction and outreach today. Explain which installation and adoption decisions still require local professionals, authorities, evidence or signed commitments.
## Completion boundary
This bundle fulfills the planning and template deliverables. Actual sites, products, quotes, legal applicability, permits, signatures, customer research and pilot outcomes are not supplied by the user and cannot be truthfully completed here. The workflow assigns each to an owner rather than marking it complete.

## Version 2 continuation prompt
Continue the framework without choosing a real pilot jurisdiction. Deepen intervention comparison, engineering verification, inclusive usability, legal routing, evidence appraisal, research ethics, funding eligibility, delivery tasks, assurance and launch decisions. Include working non-sensitive planning registers and reproducible year-by-year economics. Preserve source limits and distinguish planning readiness from actual authorization. Maintain prior draft imports and package source plus verification.

docs.title: Program decision and executive brief
docs.body:
## Recommendation
Launch a voluntary, evaluated Child-Safer Spaces program. Start with documented hazards and operational controls; consider commercial cushioning only where a specific impact hazard survives simpler remedies. Do not mandate household foam tiles or pool noodles across retail aisles.
## Purpose and scope
Reduce avoidable slips, trips, falls and collisions in entrances, aisles, queues and waiting spaces. Initial planning population: visitors under 18, with all-user and worker balancing measures. Confirm age bands and legal definitions locally. Shopping-cart falls, escalators, stairs, climbing and falling merchandise require separate controls; floor padding must not be represented as their solution. Play areas form a separate workstream.
## Decisions requested of the sponsor
- Appoint a site lead, facilities owner and independent evaluation lead.
- Authorize an assessment budget of [amount/currency] and a capped pilot budget of [amount], with separate removal reserve.
- Adopt the gate sequence and empower every worker to report and isolate hazards under the site procedure.
- Permit publication of aggregate positive, neutral and adverse findings after privacy review.
## Intervention order
First remove the hazard: repair leaks, broken transitions and obstructing fixtures. Next redesign exposure: rounded corners, better layout and secure entrance systems. Then strengthen inspection, cleaning and response. Finally evaluate cushioning where the remaining mechanism and operational conditions justify it.
## What success means
A site can demonstrate that its chosen controls are installed as specified, maintained, accessible, and monitored. A pilot can establish feasibility before it can establish injury effectiveness. Neither participation nor this workspace creates a safety certification.
## Decision record
Sponsor [role/name]; site [ID]; budget [currency/amount]; scope exclusions [ ]; authorized actions [ ]; conditions [ ]; decision date [ ]; next review [ ]; signature in controlled record [reference].

docs.title: Sequence, ownership and first-day plan
docs.body:
## Begin today
1. Sponsor appoints a site lead and authorizes assessment. Record site, country, state/province, municipality, occupancy, owner and tenant responsibilities.
2. Manager and staff walk the site with facilities; include accessible routes, wet entrances, queues and child-height fixture contact points. Correct known hazards through existing safe procedures immediately; do not preserve hazards for research.
3. Open hazard and action registers. Identify a safe alternative route for any isolated area.
4. Risk team requests existing de-identified incident trends and exposure counts. No child names or medical details go into this workspace.
5. Facilities requests local authority, accessibility and supplier reviews using the enclosed templates.
6. Finance sets assessment and removal reserves. Lead schedules a seven-day review.
## Suggested schedule — planning targets, not permission deadlines
| Gate | Window | Accountable owner | Evidence to advance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G0 Scope | Day 1–2 | Sponsor | Charter, site, roles, initial hazard controls |
| G1 Baseline | Week 1–4 or longer | Evaluation lead | Hazard map, usable exposure data, baseline limitations |
| G2 Local pathway | Before procurement commitment | Facilities lead | Adopted requirements, permits and landlord determinations |
| G3 Product suitability | Before purchase | Procurement lead | Accepted dossier, mock-up results, written test criteria |
| G4 Installation | Before public use | Site manager | Commissioning, training, maintenance and rollback readiness |
| G5 Pilot review | Weekly; formal at 90 days | Sponsor | Adverse-event review, operational data and independent analysis |
| G6 Scale | Evidence-dependent | Executive sponsor | Documented benefits/uncertainties, costs and no unresolved critical defects |
## Responsibility matrix
| Work | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Budget and stop decisions | Sponsor | Site lead | Finance, insurer |
| Legal applicability | Business legal lead | Local counsel/code professional | Authorities, landlord |
| Design and installation | Facilities lead | Designer/installer | Accessibility, fire, cleaning specialists |
| Daily controls | Site manager | Shift and cleaning teams | Worker representatives |
| Evaluation and data | Evaluation lead | Analyst/data steward | Privacy lead, community representatives |
| External claims | Communications lead | Writer | Legal and evaluation leads |
An authority decides within its remit; a consultant or insurer cannot substitute for that determination. Assign a deputy for every daily role and record handovers.

docs.title: Evidence and hazard map
docs.body:
## Evidence assessment
This is a targeted primary-source review, accessed 19 October 2026, not a systematic review or a retail-child injury meta-analysis. No quantitative child-retail benefit estimate has been established in this review. Before a large trial, commission a reproducible literature search with inclusion criteria, independent screening and product-specific evidence appraisal.
| Hazard or intervention | Evidence and relevance | Program decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wet/contaminated floor | HSE retail guidance prioritizes contamination and cleaning [S2] | Core operational workstream; monitor response and recurring sources |
| Broken or shifting surface | OSHA addresses worker surface inspection and hazard correction [S3] | Repair and inspect; establish customer obligations separately |
| Soft or unstable surface | Access Board guidance explains mobility barriers [S1] | Accessibility is a pass/fail requirement |
| Commercial compliant flooring | FLIP found no benefit for serious injuries for the studied system in older-adult long-term care [S8] | Indirect, setting-specific evidence; no inference of proven pediatric retail efficacy |
| Playground surfacing | F1292 concerns playground head-impact attenuation [S7] | Cannot establish retail fall prevention or fracture prevention |
| Rounded fixtures/edge guards | Mechanically plausible hazard reduction; no quantified retail-child effect established here | Prefer hazard removal; test guard attachment and failure modes |
## Site survey
Map each hazard by zone, mechanism, exposure, existing control, suspected injury route, photographs without people, and immediate action. Include doors, aisle ends, shelf brackets, queue barriers, mat edges, transitions, leaks and debris. Observe restocking and cleaning as well as normal trading. Review small-wheel and cane-tip interactions.
## Risk triage — proposed program method
Use severity 1–5 and likelihood 1–5 only as a prioritization aid. Describe each rating and uncertainty; multiplication is not a legal safety determination. Potentially serious hazards, blocked escape routes, loose parts and unstable walking surfaces trigger immediate isolation regardless of score. Lower-risk improvements receive an owner and due date; overdue actions escalate to the site manager.
## Evidence gaps to commission
Pediatric retail incidence by mechanism; representative loaded-cart and mobility testing; aged and wet installation performance; guard durability; cleaning compatibility; life-cycle costs; comparative injury outcomes. Assign these questions before claiming effectiveness.

docs.title: Stakeholder appeal and adoption strategy
docs.body:
## Value propositions to validate
| Audience | Proposed appeal | Proof needed | First ask |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Parents/caregivers | Fewer avoidable hazards during daily visits | Visible fixes, credible reporting, honest limits | Review a walk-through and feedback survey |
| Disabled visitors/older adults | Safer routes without extra mobility effort | User involvement, accessible transitions and routes | Paid adult accessibility advisory session |
| Store staff | Clear response duties and fewer repeat hazards | Workable time, training and repair support | Join shift walkthrough and usability trial |
| Business leadership | Manageable risk and predictable total costs | Budget, operating feasibility and measured outcomes | Fund a bounded pilot |
| Insurer/self-insured risk team | Auditable prevention and reliable data | Exposure-adjusted trends, maintenance and product evidence | Agree review and evidence criteria |
| Government/public health | Prevention with equitable access | Independent results and feasible enforcement | Support evaluation and coordination |
| Suppliers/landlords | Clear specifications and responsibility | Traceable acceptance and maintenance terms | Provide dossier and written permissions |
## Adoption sequence
Recruit one sponsor and a small set of suitable sites; engage disability representatives and staff before selecting products. Agree evidence questions with insurer and authorities, then obtain competing supplier responses. Publish a factual pilot notice. Review operational findings at 30, 60 and 90 days. Expand only after Gate G6; replication should include different exposure and store sizes.
## Selection rubric
Score each site 0–2 for documented hazard burden, data quality, management capacity, representative traffic, feasible comparison, and ability to isolate/revert changes. These are program screening scores, not risk certifications. Exclude sites unable to maintain a safe accessible route or fund removal. Include smaller businesses when maintenance capacity can be supported.
## Prevent adoption friction
Offer standard documents, shared testing, training time and procurement options. Keep public claims specific. Do not promise lower premiums, tax credits, grants or a universal return on investment. A large retailer is an example, not an assumed partner.

docs.title: Jurisdiction and obligation register
docs.body:
## Four distinct requirement types
LAW: a binding rule applicable to this site. CONTRACT: a lease, insurer or purchase obligation. PROGRAM: an internal criterion adopted for this pilot. PROPOSAL: an incentive or future policy request. Record the type, citation, edition, scope, decision-maker and evidence for every requirement.
## U.S. starting map
| Topic | Initial reference | Local action and owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accessibility | ADA surface guidance [S1] | Accessibility professional/counsel confirms federal scope and state/local rules |
| Employee surface safety | OSHA 1910.22 [S3] | Safety lead confirms federal or state-plan regime |
| Building/fire/egress | Adopted state/local codes | Code professional identifies occupancy, alteration classification, material tests and permits |
| Retail food areas | FDA model code [S4] | Health authority identifies adopted edition, amendments and affected areas |
| Product flammability | CPSC framework [S12] | Supplier/counsel classifies material and required documentation |
| Customer injury liability | State law and facts | Local counsel maps duties, preservation and claims notices |
## Canada starting map
Provinces/territories and local authorities determine applicable building and fire rules. NRC lists 2025 model publications [S6]; the archived FAQ explains adoption [S5]. Neither establishes the edition at a particular site. Confirm provincial accessibility/human-rights requirements, worker safety regime, occupiers' liability, public-health requirements and applicable privacy law with local specialists. Do not apply U.S. ADA numerical rules as Canadian legal requirements.
## Required site record before G2
Site/address [ ]; jurisdiction [ ]; occupancy/use [ ]; work description [ ]; adopted code and amendments [ ]; section [ ]; applicability reasoning [ ]; permit yes/no/undetermined [ ]; issuing authority [ ]; responsible professional [ ]; evidence reference [ ]; inspection stage [ ]; expiry/recheck date [ ]. Every 'not applicable' requires a documented reason and reviewer.
## Open items
No site jurisdiction was provided. This is a localization framework, not a completed compliance opinion. Obtain written determinations before modifying regulated assemblies, escape routes, food areas or required accessible routes. Recheck after design, occupancy or code changes.

docs.title: Authority consultation and approval request
docs.body:
## Draft request — adapt and send through the organization's normal channel
Subject: Pre-installation review request — Child-Safer Spaces pilot at [site]

We are assessing [specific hazards] at [address, occupancy, tenant/owner]. The proposed work comprises [surface system, edge protection, extent, substrate, attachment, transitions]. We request guidance on the applicable adopted requirements, permit pathway and inspections before purchase or installation.

Attached: marked plan and accessible/egress routes; existing and proposed dimensions; product and assembly dossier; fire and surface test reports; installation/adhesive details; sanitation and maintenance procedure; landlord consent status; commissioning plan and rollback design.

Please identify: applicable code edition/amendments and sections; whether the work constitutes a regulated alteration; required drawings or professional seals; fire-performance test/classification for this assembly and location; accessibility review; health review for relevant zones; permits and inspection hold points; and any conditions or additional evidence needed. Please indicate any issue outside your authority and the correct office to consult.

Contact: [authorized project contact]. Intended dates: [ ]. We will not treat silence or receipt as approval. We can revise or withdraw the proposed system if required.
## Meeting record
Authority/office [ ]; official [ ]; date [ ]; remit [ ]; questions [ ]; answer and cited basis [ ]; written response reference [ ]; unresolved matters [ ]; action owner/date [ ]; next submission [ ].
## Separate decision log
Record submitted, additional information requested, conditional approval, approved, rejected or not required with written basis. Do not combine building, fire, accessibility and health permissions into a single unsupported 'compliant' field. Approval for one site or product configuration does not transfer automatically to another.

docs.title: Performance specification and acceptance schedule
docs.body:
## Procurement principle
Specify the whole installed system: surface, underlay, seams, trims, adhesive, substrate, fixtures and cleaning method. Any substitution reopens review. Test thresholds must be written and approved before testing, not selected after results are seen.
| Attribute | Required supplier evidence | Site acceptance decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slip behavior | Named method, device validation, wet/dry and relevant contaminants, lab/field conditions | Independent specialist sets method-specific threshold and site verification |
| Firmness/stability/access | Deformation, secured edges, transition details; full-scale mock-up | Accessibility professional accepts routes and mobility performance |
| Fire | Assembly report with thickness, adhesive and substrate represented | Code professional/authority confirms applicable test, class and location |
| Rolling/static loads | Loaded carts, stocking equipment, displays and cleaning machinery | No unacceptable rutting, delamination, effort or instability under approved cycles |
| Durability | Aged/abraded/wet results, seam and bond data | Criteria, sampling and retest interval fixed in test plan |
| Hygiene | Compatible chemicals, drying, seams, spill ingress, replaceability | Cleaning lead and health authority where relevant accept demonstration |
| Edge guards | Attachment, tear resistance, projections, small detached parts, reach | Designer accepts no new snag, ingestion, detachment or collision hazard |
| Impact mitigation | Relevant geometry, energies, body-region surrogate, limits | Specialist accepts method; no unsupported injury-reduction translation |
| Materials | Traceability, composition disclosures, applicable chemical/emission evidence and SDS where applicable | Relevant product/indoor-air restrictions checked locally |
## Accessibility detail
Under the U.S. ADA guidance, accessible surfaces must be firm, stable and slip resistant; level changes up to 1/4 inch can be untreated, and up to 1/2 inch require appropriate beveling. Larger changes need compliant treatment. There is no universal ADA friction coefficient [S1]. Check the actual standard, scope and more restrictive local rules before design approval.
## Mandatory acceptance fields
Attribute [ ]; method/version [ ]; sample/system [ ]; conditioning [ ]; threshold and rationale [ ]; approving specialist [ ]; laboratory [ ]; report [ ]; result [ ]; pass/fail/undetermined [ ]; corrective action [ ]. Any critical undetermined criterion blocks public installation.

docs.title: Supplier RFI, bid comparison and purchase terms
docs.body:
## Request for information
Provide product name/version, intended commercial application, exclusions, full assembly, thickness, seams, substrate conditions, installation instructions, cure time, cleaning requirements, service life assumptions, disposal route and warranty. Supply independent reports with laboratory scope/accreditation where relevant, sample identity, dates, methods, conditions, failures and limitations. Identify differences between tested and offered systems.
Quote quantities and unit basis, preparation, moisture testing, labor, closures, taxes, freight, training, spare stock, inspections, periodic tests, repairs and removal. State currency, validity, lead time, warranty remedy and who bears failed acceptance costs. Disclose conflicts and funding of studies. Do not describe a product as 'childproof' or rely solely on playground certification.
## Comparison process
First pass/fail the mandatory legal, fire, accessibility, hygiene, stability and operational criteria. A cheaper bid cannot offset failure. For surviving bids use proposed weights: operating suitability 30%, durability/maintenance 25%, whole-life cost 25%, relevant independent evidence 15%, support/traceability 5%. Score 0–5 with written reasons; retain dissent and missing evidence. Adjust weights before seeing bids.
## Draft purchase schedule for contract review
- Approved assembly and exact manufacturer/version: [ ]. No substitution without written reapproval.
- Installer competence and insurance evidence: [ ]. Work area and reopening conditions: [ ].
- Hold points: substrate acceptance, concealed work inspection, commissioning and final acceptance.
- Defect/removal responsibilities, response times and payment holdback: [negotiated terms].
- Warranty covers [ ]; exclusions [ ]; remedy [ ]; labor/removal costs [ ].
- Batch/lot traceability, recall notice and product-change notice: [ ].
- Required handover documents, spare materials, training and ongoing service: [ ].
- Indemnity, liability allocation, governing law and insurance terms: counsel to draft for actual parties.
This is a commercial term sheet, not an executed contract. Keep an approved alternative and a funded removal plan.

docs.title: Pilot charter and operating agreement
docs.body:
## Charter fields
Project [ ]; sponsor [ ]; site IDs and addresses [ ]; participating entities [ ]; problem statement with baseline reference [ ]; intervention and comparator [ ]; affected zones [ ]; exclusions [ ]; start/end/review dates [ ]; budget/currency [ ]; removal reserve [ ]; success and stop criteria [ ]; document version [ ].
## Agreed commitments
The operator maintains ordinary safety controls at every participating site, supplies staff time and logs, and promptly addresses reported hazards. The facilities lead owns design and product configuration. The evaluation lead predefines measures and independently reviews results. The supplier supports traceability, failure investigation and warranty obligations. Disability and community advisors review practical access and communication; participation does not make them guarantors of safety.
## Governance
Weekly site review examines open defects, exposure completeness, incidents, mobility concerns and cost. Monthly steering review includes sponsor, operations, facilities, accessibility, evaluation and risk leads. Declare supplier funding and conflicts; persons with a commercial interest do not independently approve their own product evidence.
## Decision rights
Any trained worker may initiate the site's hazard isolation process. The manager controls closure and emergency escalation. Restart requires the owners listed in document 14, plus authorities when relevant. Only the sponsor can authorize scope or budget increases; approval cannot waive applicable legal requirements.
## Data and publication
Keep claims and personal records in the organization's protected system. Share only agreed aggregate or appropriately de-identified data. Publish methods, denominators, adverse effects, costs and uncertainty; do not suppress neutral findings. Privacy and legal review govern release.
## Signatures and unresolved conditions
Operator [ ]; property owner [ ]; facilities [ ]; evaluation [ ]; supplier [ ]; date [ ]; conditions precedent [ ]; separate legally executed agreement reference [ ]. Store signed records under document control. Workspace checkboxes are reminders, not signatures.

docs.title: Installation and commissioning checklist
docs.body:
## Before work
Confirm G0–G3 evidence, permits, landlord consent, accepted drawings and tested assembly. Record installer competence, work schedule and safe public separation. Confirm storage, ventilation/cure instructions and removal materials. Inspect substrate moisture, flatness, damage and contamination against supplier criteria. Record failures before covering them.
## During installation
Capture batch/lot numbers, surface preparation, adhesive quantities, cure conditions, seam and trim configuration, and any deviations. Keep access and escape routes open or implement an approved alternative. Protect adjacent fixtures and food-related operations. Do not accept unreviewed substitutions to solve a schedule problem.
## Before public reopening
- Verify surface bond, seams, movement, transitions, openings and clearances against approved drawings.
- Verify approved cleaning method, dry condition, cure time and any required tests.
- Demonstrate mobility aids, strollers, loaded carts and cleaning equipment in a controlled setting with consenting trained adults; no deliberate falls or child impact trials.
- Check guard retention, projections, snagging, tear/detachment and cleaning access.
- Close all critical defects; record noncritical punch-list owner and deadline.
- Obtain required authority inspections; hand over as-built details, reports, warranty, spare parts, training and inspection schedule.
## Commissioning record
Site/zone [ ]; assembly/lot [ ]; installer [ ]; installed date [ ]; inspection/test references [ ]; accessibility reviewer [ ]; fire/code review [ ]; cleaning acceptance [ ]; operator acceptance [ ]; defects and closure [ ]; authorized reopening date/time [ ].
## Follow-up
Proposed checks: immediately before reopening, after first peak trading period, after first full cleaning, at one week and at one month, then risk-based. Increase checks after spills, restocking damage, complaints or unusual loading. These are program defaults requiring site approval, not universal code intervals.

docs.title: Daily inspection, cleaning and spill response SOP
docs.body:
## Owner and coverage
Site manager owns the procedure; each shift names a responder and deputy. Set inspection frequency by hazard, weather, traffic and incident history. Proposed minimum planning points: opening, shift handover, closing, and after cleaning/spills/restocking; high-risk zones need more frequent checks. Record the approved interval in the register.
## Inspection
Walk entrances, transitions, queues, aisles and guards. Check water, debris, curling, movement, seam gaps, loose parts, contamination, new projections and blocked routes. Record time, zone, defect, action and reopening verification. A blank log is not a completed inspection.
## Spill/hazard response
1. Protect people: prevent entry to the affected area and provide a safe accessible alternative; notify the shift lead. Do not block emergency escape.
2. Identify the hazard and summon the appropriate trained responder. Unknown chemicals, blood or other specialist hazards use the existing specialist procedure.
3. Remove contamination and address the source using the approved product, dilution and equipment. Keep the area isolated while wet or unsafe. HSE warns that signs alone do not prevent entry [S2].
4. Inspect dryness, residue, seams, attachment and surrounding area; record verification before reopening.
5. Log detection, isolation, cleanup and reopening times; investigate repeated sources and escalate repairs.
## Cleaning plan
List surface/zone [ ]; approved chemical and dilution [ ]; equipment [ ]; drying method [ ]; scheduled time [ ]; guard/seam inspection [ ]; waste route [ ]; responsible contractor [ ]. Do not change polish, coating, chemical or pad without compatibility review.
## Escalation
Immediately isolate lifting edges, unstable surfaces, detached guards, blocked access or sanitation failures. Escalate missed inspections, overdue repair and recurrent wetting to the manager. Document interim controls and restart under document 14. Retain records under the approved retention policy.

docs.title: Staff training and competency record
docs.body:
## Suggested 25-minute shift module
Five minutes: explain prevention versus cushioning and the actual site hazards. Five minutes: demonstrate inspection of entrances, seams, guards and routes. Ten minutes: practice a spill response and an isolation/reopening decision. Five minutes: report a concern and complete the log. Adapt language, format and duration to workers' needs; include contractors and temporary staff.
## Trainer script
Our purpose is to reduce avoidable hazards for children and everyone else. A soft surface can still slip, move or obstruct wheels. Report defects promptly. Do not improvise repairs or attach household foam to fixtures. Maintain the designated safe route. Signs warn; the site procedure determines how to keep people out of an unsafe area. Only the authorized role reopens the area after checks.
## Competency demonstration
Ask each learner to identify three hazards, isolate a simulated spill without blocking escape, locate the approved cleaning instructions, record all four response times, and identify who can authorize restart. Repeat instruction if any critical step is missed. Do not use a live dangerous spill for practice.
## Record template
Worker identifier [ ]; role/shift [ ]; trainer [ ]; date [ ]; module version [ ]; language/accommodation [ ]; demonstration passed or retraining required [ ]; retraining action/date [ ]; supervisor verification [ ]. Maintain worker records in the approved personnel system.
## Refresher triggers
New worker or contractor, changed product or cleaning process, observed unsafe practice, material failure, incident investigation finding or site-specified refresher date. Display a short job aid: Protect people → Notify → Correct using approved method → Verify → Log → Reopen by authorized role.
## Supervisor check
Observe one real inspection and review logs on a risk-based schedule. Address workload and missing supplies; do not punish good-faith reporting or use low reported incident counts as the sole performance incentive.

docs.title: Incident, stop, removal and restart protocol
docs.body:
## Incident response
Use the site's emergency response procedure and summon appropriate assistance. Staff must not diagnose injury or conduct experimental treatment. Secure the area and preserve relevant evidence through authorized processes. Notify the manager and claims contact according to existing policy deadlines; record those actual deadlines in the contact sheet.
## Immediate stop triggers — proposed program rules
Any new unstable or lifting surface; loose/detached guard or small part; blocked or materially impaired accessible/escape route; sanitation failure; installation-related fire concern; or serious incident plausibly related to the intervention triggers isolation and suspension of the affected installation pending review. These conditions do not require proof of causation before taking protective action.
## Record and investigate
Assign a coded incident ID. Capture zone, time, mechanism, observed conditions, immediate controls, witness record location and relevant product batch. Store identities, photographs showing people, footage and medical/claims information only in protected systems. Preserve originals and chain of custody; avoid speculative blame. Privacy/legal leads determine retention and legal holds.
## Withdrawal plan
Facilities arranges competent removal, restores an approved walking surface, checks substrate/adhesive residues and transitions, and manages waste under applicable instructions. Maintain the safe alternative route and closure communications. Reserve funds and removal lead time before installation. Track defects across other sites sharing the same batch or assembly; notify supplier and relevant authorities where required.
## Restart authorization
Document root-cause assessment, corrected design, retesting against pre-agreed criteria, access/fire/health review as relevant, staff retraining and revised procedure. Site manager and facilities lead sign; accessibility reviewer signs access-related corrections; authority signs where required. Sponsor authorizes continuation of the pilot. Record decision and rationale even if permanent removal is chosen.
## Contact sheet
Emergency process [ ]; duty manager/deputy [ ]; facilities [ ]; cleaning [ ]; installer [ ]; supplier recall contact [ ]; insurer claims [ ]; privacy/legal [ ]; authorities [ ]; after-hours route [ ].

docs.title: Pilot evaluation protocol
docs.body:
## Design
Stage A is operational feasibility, with a suggested 90-day observation window after commissioning. It cannot by itself establish reduced injury rates. Stage B is a larger comparative effectiveness study only if feasibility and statistical planning justify it. An independent analyst selects sample size and duration from actual baseline event rates, target effect, site clustering, exposure, attrition and acceptable uncertainty; no universal site count is asserted.
Use matched comparison sites or randomized/staged introduction where feasible. Provide standard safety corrections everywhere. Pre-register intervention components, primary outcome, analysis, stop rules and exclusions before outcome review. Record seasonal weather, promotions, traffic changes, reporting changes and concurrent renovations. A multi-component pilot estimates the package effect; it cannot isolate cushioning without a suitable component comparison.
## Outcomes
Primary effectiveness outcome proposed: reported fall events with injury per 100,000 visitor entries, all visitors. Separately report child injury events; use child-visit denominators only if measured credibly. If unavailable, label child events per total visits as a proxy, not a child incidence rate. Track fixture collisions separately from falls. Secondary measures: severity bands, all falls, near misses, mobility barriers, staff push effort, sanitation defects, response time, downtime and total cost.
## Operational acceptance targets — proposed
Zero unresolved critical defects; all required approvals recorded; staff demonstrate critical procedure steps; inspection completion target at least 95%; exposure-data completeness target at least 95%; no unresolved access or sanitation barrier. Review deviations individually; aggregate scores cannot override critical failures. Targets must be adopted locally before the pilot.
## Analysis
Report counts, exposure, missingness, rates and uncertainty. Rate ratio = intervention rate / comparison rate; it is not causal without design assumptions. For baseline changes, compare rate changes across groups and account for site clustering and trends. Have the analyst use suitable count models and confidence intervals; suppress ratios when denominators are invalid. Zero events are not proof of zero risk. Report adverse outcomes even if injury counts improve.
## Ethical oversight
Obtain the institution's research/quality-improvement determination before human research. Obtain appropriate adult participation consent and accessibility accommodations; child research needs separate ethics, consent/assent and safeguarding review. No induced falls or child impact experiments. Publish protocol deviations and conflicts.

docs.title: Data dictionary and reporting specification
docs.body:
## Definitions
| Field/measure | Definition | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Site ID, zone ID | Stable non-identifying facility and area codes | Never reuse codes |
| Fall event | Unintentional coming to rest on ground/floor or lower level | One event even if multiple injuries |
| Collision event | Contact with fixture without a fall | Keep separate; record linked fall ID if needed |
| Near miss | Loss of balance or hazard encounter without defined injury event | Separate from injury numerator |
| Age band | Under 5; 5–11; 12–17; adult; unknown | No inferred exact age; unknown stays unknown |
| Severity | No reported injury; minor reported; professional assessment reported; serious/hospital reported; unknown | Not a staff medical diagnosis; apply approved coding rules |
| Visitor entries | Measured entrances during stated period | Not unique persons; document staff exclusions and sensor outages |
| Child entries | Credible measured/estimated child visits | Document sampling and uncertainty; never infer from total visits alone |
| Inspection completion | Completed required checks / scheduled checks | Include missed checks |
| Response times | Detection→isolation, isolation→cleanup, cleanup→reopening | Use timestamps, document unknown detection time |
## Data flow
Operations records source events in the existing secure system. Data steward removes identifiers, checks duplicates and aligns time windows. Analyst receives approved aggregate data. Steering group receives rates and adverse-condition summaries. Public reports undergo small-cell and re-identification review; default proposal is suppress cells below 5 and complementary cells that reveal them, subject to privacy approval.
## Quality checks
Reconcile incident IDs, exposure periods, duplicate reports and severity updates. Missing data is not zero. Report excluded periods and reasons; audit a sample against secure originals. Retain a revision log. Calculate rates only for matching events and exposure windows.
## Monthly report template
Sites and period [ ]; intervention version [ ]; count/exposure/rate [ ]; uncertainty [ ]; child proxy caveat [ ]; near misses [ ]; critical defects [ ]; access/hygiene findings [ ]; inspection completeness [ ]; costs [ ]; limitations [ ]; corrective actions [ ]; decision [ ].

docs.title: Business case and financial model
docs.body:
## Decision approach
Use the cost of operating a verified control, with injury savings treated as uncertain. Obtain supplier quotes and actual claims analysis before investment approval. Separate insured losses from costs the business retains; do not count an insurer's payment as a business saving or add the same saving twice through premium reductions.
## Input schedule
Currency [ ]; study/assessment [ ]; design/permits [ ]; materials [ ]; substrate preparation [ ]; installation [ ]; closure [ ]; training [ ]; independent testing [ ]; contingency [ ]; removal reserve [ ]; incremental annual maintenance [ ]; annual retesting [ ]; replacements by year [ ]; annual retained addressable loss [ ]; assumed loss reduction [ ]; annual verified other savings [ ]; discount rate [ ]; evaluation horizon [ ].
## Formulas
Initial cost = all one-time implementation and assessment costs including reserve. Annual net benefit = addressable retained loss × assumed reduction + non-overlapping verified other savings − incremental annual cost. NPV = −initial cost + sum of (net benefit − replacement cost in year t)/(1 + discount rate)^t. Simple payback = initial cost / positive annual net benefit; otherwise no positive payback. This simplified model excludes tax, inflation and salvage unless explicitly added.
## Illustrative scenario only — no price quote or efficacy claim
Initial cost 15,000 currency units; annual added cost 2,000; annual retained addressable loss 20,000; horizon 5 years; discount 5%; no replacements or other savings. At 0% loss reduction, annual net benefit is −2,000 and NPV about −23,659. At 10%, net is 0 and NPV −15,000. At 25%, net is 3,000 and NPV about −2,012. Simple payback at 25% is 5 years, while discounted recovery takes longer. Five-year discounted break-even reduction is about 27.3% under these assumptions; it is not a predicted effect.
## Sensitivities and approval
Vary reduction, service life, replacement, maintenance burden and disruption. Include a downside case with higher losses or access problems. Record who owns costs and benefits. Approve pilot spending for evidence generation only if the sponsor accepts the possibility of no financial return.

## Extended scenarios
Document 44 and the version 2 calculator add explicit escalation, scheduled replacement and terminal salvage. The original example above remains a constant-cash-flow illustration. Existing conditional accessibility tax mechanisms are described in document 37; no eligibility is assumed.

docs.title: Privacy, records and information governance
docs.body:
## Workspace boundary
This offline HTML tool stores optional planning edits in browser storage and exports plain JSON. It has no accounts, encryption, shared audit trail or access controls. Do not enter child identities, injury narratives, health information, witness details, CCTV, claims records or confidential contracts. Use approved organizational systems for those records; store only non-sensitive document references here.
## Data minimization
Collect only information needed for the stated safety/evaluation purpose. The Canadian privacy regulator describes limiting collection under PIPEDA [S13]; applicability and other national/state/provincial requirements need local review. Do not assume consent alone satisfies all obligations. Avoid new child tracking, facial recognition or unnecessary video collection.
## Required decisions before data collection
Data owner [ ]; purpose [ ]; lawful basis/consent determination [ ]; data fields [ ]; permitted users [ ]; storage location [ ]; retention period [ ]; legal-hold process [ ]; deletion method [ ]; individual rights contact [ ]; breach response owner [ ]; sharing agreements [ ]; cross-border transfer assessment [ ]; ethics determination [ ]. Counsel/privacy officer must set actual retention periods for this site; this template does not invent a universal period.
## Access and release
Limit raw records to authorized incident/claims staff. Analysts use approved de-identified extracts. Review small groups and combinations that could reveal a family or employee. No names or identifiable photos in public reports. Keep consent separate from safety assistance and do not condition assistance on research participation.
## Local planning backup
Export planning JSON after each session to an approved location. Anyone with the file can read it. Imports replace the local planning state after confirmation; validate and back up first. Browser data may disappear when clearing site data or moving the HTML file. Different devices and origins do not synchronize. Prefer named dated exports and a single assigned editor.

docs.title: Insurer and broker review package
docs.body:
## Draft review request

We request your written comments on relevant coverage conditions, notice obligations, claims documentation, product/contractor responsibilities, and the evidence you would need to evaluate any risk recognition. We are not assuming a premium reduction or that your review constitutes regulatory approval.
## Meeting questions
- Which losses are addressable and which are outside this intervention's mechanism?
- What loss-development period, severity data and exposure denominator would support a credible comparison?
- Does the proposed installation or trial require notification, endorsement or underwriting review under our actual policy?
- What exclusions, deductibles, retentions, reporting deadlines and contractor requirements need counsel/broker attention?

Policy review reference [ ]; claims summary [ ]; site map [ ]; technical dossier [ ]; approvals [ ]; operations procedure [ ]; training [ ]; maintenance logs [ ]; adverse-event record [ ]; independent report [ ]; costs [ ].

docs.title: Government and public-health proposal
docs.body:
## Policy brief
Problem: everyday commercial environments contain preventable walking and fixture hazards; child-specific retail benefit from cushioning remains unestablished in this review. Proposal: support a voluntary, material-neutral demonstration program with independent evaluation and accessible design.
## Requested actions — proposals, not existing entitlements
1. Convene building, fire, accessibility, public-health, business, labor, disability and injury-prevention representatives.
2. Publish a common assessment and evidence framework without specifying one material.
3. Invite competitively selected pilots with public methods, cost reporting and adverse-effect disclosure.
4. Consider capped small-business technical assistance, testing vouchers or grants subject to legal authority and funding.
5. Demonstrate suitable measures in public-facing procurement where permitted.
6. Review whether evidence justifies future requirements through the normal consultation and rulemaking process.
## Draft funding concept
Program sponsor [ ]; authority/funding source [ ]; total budget [ ]; eligible sites [ ]; eligible costs [assessment, design, independent tests, accessibility participation, evaluation, approved work]; maximum award [ ]; matching contribution [ ]; milestones [ ]; procurement/conflict rules [ ]; audit and repayment terms [ ]. Funding should not depend solely on positive injury results; it should require honest reporting and safe conduct.
## Proposed evaluation criteria
Need and exposure 25%; practical maintenance capacity 20%; accessibility and community participation 20%; evaluation quality 20%; cost and replicability 15%. These are proposed selection weights. Require independent review and exclude unverified product marketing.
## Decision before stronger policy
Assess effect size and uncertainty, unintended harms, implementation cost, burden on small businesses, enforcement capacity, accessible alternatives and equity. Compare to enhanced existing controls. Any future performance requirement needs locally valid methods and reasonable transition arrangements; a blanket foam mandate is not supported by this package.
## Submission cover fields
Submitting organization [ ]; requested meeting/decision [ ]; evidence references [ ]; requested funding [ ]; responsible lead [ ]; publication commitment [ ]; unresolved research [ ].

docs.title: Manufacturer, laboratory and installer work order
docs.body:
## Work order scope
Client [ ]; site [ ]; product/system revision [ ]; laboratory/installer [ ]; quotation reference [ ]; approved drawings [ ]; sample selection [ ]; methods/editions [ ]; acceptance criteria [ ]; schedule [ ]; deliverables [ ]; named reviewer [ ].
## Laboratory brief
Test representative as-installed assemblies, including substrate, adhesive, joints and trims where relevant. Document sample provenance, conditioning, aging, contamination, equipment calibration/validation, measurement uncertainty, deviations and raw results. Distinguish accredited methods from bespoke engineering tests and state limitations. Agree conditions and pass criteria with the relevant specialists before testing.
## Standards routing
F2508 concerns walkway tribometry validation [S10]; it does not provide one universal pass number for every floor. E648 addresses floor-covering critical radiant flux [S11]; the required method, classification and edition depend on the adopted code and installation. F1292-26 has a playground scope [S7]; use it only for a justified relevant application, not retail certification. Obtain licensed current/adopted texts as needed; the public summaries reviewed here do not replace test procedures.
## Installer hold points
Verify substrate and environment before work; submit deviations before proceeding; inspect concealed components; retain batch and installation records; protect public routes; meet cure and commissioning requirements. Provide removal instructions that restore a compliant surface.
## Supplier change and recall control
Notify the buyer of changes to composition, thickness, adhesive, source factory or installation instructions that could affect performance. List installed sites and batches in the asset register. Define notice recipients, defect response times, spare-stock availability and recall/removal costs in the contract.
## Completion evidence
Signed report [ ]; sample/configuration match [ ]; independent review [ ]; installer handover [ ]; acceptance/defects [ ]; payment milestone [ ]; ongoing obligations [ ]. Product certification alone does not validate every installed site.
