docs.title: Public explanation and communications kit
docs.body:
## Customer notice — replace fields before use
We are improving everyday walking areas at [site]. Our work focuses on identifying hazards, keeping routes clear, responding to spills and checking selected design improvements. Some measures are being evaluated in a limited pilot. Please tell a staff member about a loose edge, wet floor or difficulty moving through an area. For urgent assistance, use [site assistance route]. Feedback contact: [accessible channel].
This program does not make an area injury-proof. We will review maintenance, accessibility, customer feedback and incidents before deciding whether to expand it.
## FAQ
Why not cover all floors in foam? Softer materials can introduce movement, seams, cleaning difficulties or mobility resistance. We select controls for the actual hazard and test the installed system.
Does this mean injuries will fall by a certain percentage? No local reduction has yet been demonstrated. We will report findings and limitations.
Is this a certification? No. Participation describes a safety-improvement process, not an independent certification or government endorsement.
How can disabled visitors contribute? Contact [channel] for accessible feedback or a voluntary advisory session. Safe access must remain available during work.
## Business announcement draft
[Organization] is beginning a bounded Child-Safer Spaces pilot at [locations]. The pilot will assess [specific controls] alongside maintenance, accessibility and operational measures. [Evaluation organization, only if confirmed] will review [scope]. Findings, including limitations, will inform future decisions. No injury-prevention guarantee or insurance saving is being claimed.
## Claims approval checklist
Verify each factual statement against a dated record. Obtain permission before naming partners or displaying logos. Do not use 'childproof,' 'zero risk,' 'certified safe,' unsupported percentage benefits or implied insurer/government endorsement. Communications and evaluation leads approve publication; legal reviews material claims. Offer translated and accessible formats appropriate to the site.

docs.title: Adult stakeholder interview and feedback forms
docs.body:
## Recruitment and consent introduction
We are seeking voluntary feedback from adult caregivers, disabled customers, older customers and staff about walking routes and proposed improvements. This is feedback, not a safety test. You may skip questions or stop. Do not provide a child's name or medical details. Personal incidents should go through the site's protected reporting channel. Explain any recording, retention and compensation before consent.
## Caregiver/customer questions
1. Which areas are hardest to navigate, and when?
2. What makes you feel confident that hazards are handled?
3. Looking at [neutral description of proposed change], what seems useful and what concerns you?
4. Would it affect your ability to use a mobility aid, stroller or cart? How?
5. How would you prefer to report a concern?
6. What evidence would you need before believing the change improves safety?
7. Is there anything missing from this proposal?
## Staff/manager questions
What recurring hazards are hardest to control? Which shift conditions matter? Can the proposed inspection/cleaning work fit available staffing? What tools or training are missing? What would prompt you to stop use? What maintenance cost or disruption would make this impractical?
## Insurer/government questions
What evidence is necessary for your decision? Which approvals or constraints are often missed? Which parts could be standardized? What incentives are within your authority, and what would require new policy or funding?
## Proposed discovery sample and analysis
Start with approximately 5–8 adults in each relevant group as qualitative discovery, with disability representation and varied visit times. This is a convenience sample, not representative polling. Report group counts, recruitment, nonresponse and themes, including objections. Do not describe preference percentages as population estimates. Revise messages and design, then test with new participants.
## Feedback log
Date [ ]; group [ ]; channel [ ]; theme [ ]; barrier [ ]; proposed action [ ]; owner [ ]; resolution shared [ ]. Keep identifying contact information separately with permission.

docs.title: Scale, pause or stop decision memo
docs.body:
## Decision options
STOP/REMOVE when critical risks remain or the system is unsuitable. REVISE when an addressable failure needs redesign and retesting. EXTEND EVALUATION when operations are acceptable but injury evidence is insufficient. SCALE IN STAGES only when the evidence, local approvals, capacity and funding support it. Operational feasibility alone supports further testing, not a proven injury-reduction claim.
## Required evidence summary
Sites, periods and exposure [ ]; intervention configuration [ ]; comparator [ ]; primary outcome and uncertainty [ ]; adverse outcomes [ ]; accessibility findings [ ]; cleaning and worker effort [ ]; defects and maintenance [ ]; total cost [ ]; protocol deviations [ ]; conflicts [ ]; missing data [ ]; independent review [ ].
## Gate G6 questions
- Were the intended controls actually used and maintained?
- Are all critical defects and required approvals resolved?
- Are gains distinguishable from reporting, exposure or seasonal changes?
- Does the study support effectiveness, or only feasibility?
- Do child-specific data support any child-specific claim?
- Can new sites replicate the tested configuration and maintenance?
- Are removal, replacement, staff time and independent oversight funded?
- What uncertainty or adverse evidence argues against expansion?
## Controlled expansion plan
Define a new cohort, site eligibility and budget cap; repeat jurisdiction and commissioning reviews for every site. Maintain a configuration register and change notices. Monitor weekly initially and at locally approved intervals thereafter. Reopen the decision after adverse trends, material substitution, new evidence or changed use.
## Decision record
Decision [ ]; rationale [ ]; conditions [ ]; dissent [ ]; sponsor [ ]; facilities [ ]; accessibility [ ]; evaluation [ ]; legal/risk [ ]; date [ ]; next review/expiry [ ]; published summary reference [ ]. Retain unfavorable results. Do not create a safety badge without a separate credible certification governance and surveillance program.

docs.title: Repository, document control and bundle guide
docs.body:
## Version 2 guide
Version 2.0; issued 19 October 2026. Open index.html after extracting the full bundle. The workspace includes 48 documents, role navigation, search, editable templates, implementation tasks, sequential gate tracking, editable planning registers, financial scenarios, evidence and sources.

## Records and limits
This is an offline, single-user planning tool. It has no authentication, encryption, tamper-resistant audit trail, organizational approvals or live collaboration. Never store sensitive incident, medical, child, witness, claims or contract information. Browser edits and CSV records are planning copies; official evidence and signatures remain in controlled systems.

## Saving and transfer
Document drafts autosave locally; explicit Save is also available. Export a JSON backup regularly. Import validates and previews a backup before replacement, preserving the current state until you apply it. Version 1 backups can migrate. Browser storage may be unavailable or lost; exports are plain readable files. Different file paths/origins and devices do not synchronize. Calculator inputs and draft registers are included in version 2 backups.

## Print and source
The original handbook and role packs are static issue copies. Print or download a current document to include local edits. Use Print current working handbook to include saved local document edits. CSV exports include current planning rows; blank templates remain in registers. The source folder contains the content JSON, build instructions and tests. The application itself has no build/runtime dependency.

## Document control
Assign owner, approver, version, effective date and review date when adopting a procedure. Recheck after incidents, design/material/cleaning changes, new evidence or new rules. All sample records under examples are fictional and separate from live data. See VERIFICATION.md for software checks and remaining limits.

## Completion boundary
The pack supplies the general framework and adaptable work products. It does not supply a selected site, local legal opinion, approved product, signed commitments, insurer concession, grant award, ethics approval or demonstrated injury benefit. Documents 45 and 48 explain the remaining implementation decisions.

docs.title: Intervention comparison and selection library
docs.body:
## Substantive solution
Adopt a layered program in which each intervention answers a documented mechanism. Spend first on recurring contamination, damaged walking surfaces, obstructed routes and avoidable fixture geometry. Test a purpose-designed protective system only after considering removal, repair, relocation and redesign. Use the same access, fire, hygiene and durability gates for every material.
## Candidate comparison — engineering recommendations, not comparative efficacy estimates
| Candidate | Mechanism and suitable use | Main failure risks | Evidence before adoption | Position |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Leak/source repair | Stops recurrent wetting | Incomplete repair; water rerouted elsewhere | Dry-weather/wet-weather inspection, repair acceptance | First priority where applicable |
| Entrance water management | Reduces tracked-in contamination | Saturation, curled mats, inadequate coverage, threshold conflict | Drainage/mat layout, saturation management and traffic checks | Core site-specific control |
| Repair/replace damaged finish | Removes trip and surface defects | Poor bond, moisture, new transitions | Substrate investigation, approved finish and commissioning | Core remediation |
| Floor treatment/coating | Changes traction | Wears off, chemical mismatch, misleading lab rating | Relevant-condition testing and reapplication plan | Conditional; not a cure for leaks |
| Rounded/recessed fixtures | Removes or reduces contact geometry | New reach/clearance issues, structural modification | Manufacturer/designer approval and route review | Preferred design option |
| Commercial edge guard | May reduce local contact severity | Detachment, tearing, added projection, inaccessible cleaning | Actual attachment and aging/cleaning evidence | Bounded candidate for residual hazard |
| Resilient commercial flooring | May provide some impact attenuation | Rolling effort, deformation, joints, fire/cleaning behavior | Complete assembly and relevant impact evidence | Evaluate case by case |
| Engineered underlay with finish | Separates wearing layer and cushioning | Assembly mismatch, moisture trapping, substrate movement | Tested system with finish/underlay/adhesive/substrate | Requires system-level engineering |
| Interlocking household foam | Potential cushioning | Loose seams, uplift, loading, sanitation and fire uncertainty | Commercial system evidence not normally established by domestic labeling | Not default retail specification |
| Pool noodles on fixtures | Informal padding concept | Weak attachment, tearing/loose parts, unverified behavior | Redesign as purpose-engineered commercial assembly | Do not improvise an installation |
| Playground surfacing | Playground fall exposure | Wrong scope in retail and operational conflicts | Separate play-area design and applicable standards | Separate workstream [S7] |
## Selection worksheet
Hazard ID [ ]; mechanism [ ]; users/exposure [ ]; options including no capital work [ ]; elimination option [ ]; mandatory failures [ ]; supporting evidence [ ]; cost/maintenance comparison [ ]; preferred candidate [ ]; residual risks [ ]; independent reviewer [ ]; next gate [ ]. A scored preference never overrides a failed mandatory criterion.
## Zone examples
Grocery entrance: investigate water source, entrance coverage and cleaning response before cushioning. Dry toy-store aisle: inspect transitions and displays; avoid suggesting padding makes climbing safe. Queue: relocate sharp contact points and preserve maneuvering/escape space. Restaurant: zoning and sanitation compatibility may dominate floor selection. These are design starting points, not site specifications.

docs.title: Site assessment and exposure-mapping workbook
docs.body:
## Prepare the assessment
Owner: site lead with facilities and worker participation. Gather a floor plan, trading and cleaning schedules, de-identified incident mechanisms, maintenance history, known access concerns and planned renovations. Invite disability advisors through an accessible voluntary process. Do not stage hazards or ask children to demonstrate falls.
## Site profile form
Site code [ ]; country [ ]; state/province/territory [ ]; municipality [ ]; occupancy/business type [ ]; tenant/owner [ ]; operating hours [ ]; typical/peak visitor entries [ ]; counting method [ ]; worker shifts [ ]; food/play zones [ ]; stocking equipment [ ]; landlord restrictions [ ]; emergency plan reference [ ].
## Walk each zone at different operating states
Observe opening, peak traffic, cleaning, restocking and wet weather where safely feasible. Record whether the assessed condition is observed, reported or inferred. Walk at adult eye level and inspect lower fixture contact zones without assuming one child height represents all users. Record route width and transition measurements for specialist review; do not use a guessed dimension as a compliance conclusion.
| Zone | Observe | Required record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exterior/entrance | Rain paths, drainage, mat coverage, threshold and drying | Weather, location, water source, maintenance owner |
| Aisles/endcaps | Display bases, packages, carts, projections and visibility | Plan reference, obstruction source, restocking time |
| Queues/service | Crowd pinch points, turns, fixtures, maneuvering | Busy-period configuration and alternative route |
| Food-adjacent | Grease, spills, cleaning residues and ingress below finish | Contaminant, method, affected food zone |
| Equipment routes | Loaded wheels, turning, braking, stationary loads | Equipment mass/loading and wheel/contact data |
| Separate play area | Boundaries and specialist requirements | Separate design owner; no retail-floor substitution |
## Hazard register completion
Write an observable condition: 'entrance mat edge lifting at northwest corner after cart traffic' rather than 'unsafe floor.' Record immediate containment, responsible role, permanent remedy, due date, verification and recurrence check. Critical conditions are isolated immediately; remaining assessment work continues elsewhere.
## Exposure protocol
Count entries over the same time and zones as events. Record sensor placement, exclusion of staff/re-entry, outages and manual validation samples. If only whole-store counts exist, report whole-store rates; do not label them zone-specific rates. Child denominators need a separately approved credible measurement method. No facial recognition or identity tracking is required.
## Review output
Rank recurring mechanisms, identify incomplete records, select one bounded intervention area and a comparable area/site, and issue a signed assessment summary. Retain photographs without people and a dated plan as evidence references in controlled storage.

docs.title: Verification test plan and laboratory acceptance form
docs.body:
## Test plan must precede testing
Plan ID/version [ ]; system and intended zone [ ]; commissioning owner [ ]; test designer [ ]; independent lab [ ]; manufacturer [ ]; relevant authority requirements [ ]; specimen selection [ ]; approved acceptance schedule [ ]; conflicts [ ]. Numerical limits left unresolved by the source evidence must be set by competent specialists before ordering a public installation.
## Test matrix
| Test family | Conditions to specify | Results and pass decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Traction | Dry; water; representative contaminants; actual cleaning residue; aged surface; direction | Method/version, instrument validity, readings, uncertainty and site-specific acceptance |
| Seams/edges | New and aged; loaded crossing/turning; wetting/cleaning cycles | Gap/uplift/movement, bond failure, defect photographs and disposition |
| Static/rolling load | Maximum intended load, wheel type/contact area, turning radius, cycles and dwell | Residual indentation, delamination, rolling force and recovery time |
| Attachment | Exact guard/substrate/adhesive/fastener; foreseeable cleaning/contact abuse | Detachment, tearing, exposed fastener, loose parts and geometry |
| Cleanability | Actual soil, chemical, machine/pad, dilution, drying and seam access | Residue/ingress/damage observations and specialist-selected sanitation verification |
| Fire performance | Actual floor or fixture assembly and intended location | Required code test/classification and report applicability |
| Impact attenuation | Relevant surrogate/geometry, energy, substrate and conditioning | Measured force/acceleration and uncertainty; limited to tested mechanism |
| Access/ergonomics | Routes, transitions, wheels, cane tips, turns, start/stop and loaded equipment | Specialist/user review with predefined tolerances and stop rules |
## Sampling and evidence integrity
Lab proposes replicate numbers based on method, variability and decision confidence; record why samples represent production lots. Record instrument identifiers and calibration, environmental conditions, specimen thickness and full assembly. Keep failures and raw observations, not only a favorable mean. Test worn/cleaned systems where expected aging could change performance. Retest after composition or installation changes.
## Acceptance form
Criterion [ ]; required value/qualitative condition [ ]; source of requirement [law/program/contract]; approving specialist/date [ ]; test report [ ]; actual result and uncertainty [ ]; pass/fail/undetermined [ ]; deviations [ ]; corrective action [ ]; independent reviewer [ ]. The most favorable test result does not override an unfavorable safety result.
## Limits
F2508 addresses tribometry validation [S10]. It does not convert a friction reading into a guaranteed injury rate. Laboratory impact attenuation is a surrogate outcome; retail-child injury prevention remains to be evaluated. Never substitute a playground laboratory claim for whole-system operational acceptance.

## Candidate methods register — applicability to be determined
| Topic | Candidate reference | Required qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamic rolling loads | ASTM F2753-21 public scope [S25] | Relevant to resilient systems, including component combinations and joints; specify actual equipment/loading and obtain applicable text |
| Canadian surface burning | CAN/ULC-S102.2 public listing [S26] | Code professional confirms required edition, class, assembly and location; not interchangeable with a U.S. fire test by assumption |
| Canadian accessible design | CSA/ASC B651 [S27] | Determine whether adopted or a program criterion; do not substitute it for applicable provincial requirements |
| U.S. floor-covering fire method | ASTM E648 [S11] | Required edition/class established by applicable code and system |
| Tribometry validation | ASTM F2508 [S10] | Instrument/method relevance; not a universal safe friction number |
| Playground attenuation | ASTM F1292 [S7] | Separate play-area scope; no retail or all-injury certification inference |

A public listing identifies a method, not a completed compliance assessment. Record required versus latest edition, licensed text, reviewer, approved threshold and report in the standards register.

docs.title: Inclusive access and worker-ergonomics review
docs.body:
## Purpose
Assess whether the intervention preserves safe and dignified movement for all users. Legal access review and practical usability review are complementary; neither a satisfied volunteer nor a code checklist alone establishes all-user suitability.
## Planning requirements
Accessibility professional [ ]; worker ergonomics reviewer [ ]; adult advisory participants [voluntary, compensated as agreed]; accessible briefing format [ ]; privacy/ethics determination [ ]; tested configuration [ ]; comparator [ ]; predefined stop criteria [ ]. Provide a safe option to decline and stop; never ask a person to attempt an obviously hazardous route.
## Controlled mock-up tasks
First inspect physical configuration without users. Then, if accepted for testing, trained consenting adults assess approach, entry, straight travel, turning, stopping, fixture reach and exit. Include representative manual/powered wheelchairs, walkers, canes, strollers and loaded carts as appropriate. Do not claim a few devices represent every user. No induced slips or falls, no child impact trials and no excessive exertion.
## Measurement sheet
Task [ ]; device/wheel configuration [ ]; loading [ ]; surface/transition [ ]; direction [ ]; baseline and proposed condition [ ]; measured starting/sustained force where professionally specified [ ]; self-reported effort/discomfort [ ]; assistance required [ ]; snag/instability [ ]; action [ ]. Randomize task order if appropriate to reduce learning/fatigue effects; provide rest and record incomplete tasks.
## Review conditions
Predetermine tolerances with the relevant professional rather than inventing a universal acceptable percentage of added push force. Inability to navigate, wheel/cane trapping, unexpected instability, pain, fatigue concerns or a new barrier triggers suspension of that test and review. A smooth alternate route must not become an inferior, obstructed or segregating service route.
## Fixture and visual review
Check added guard thickness, circulation-path projections, cane detection, visual contrast, glare and patterns that could be misread as steps or holes. U.S. protruding-object guidance applies to circulation paths and distinguishes detectable geometry [S24]. Review local requirements and real fixture layout; cushioning can worsen projection hazards.
## Sign-off
Physical compliance review [ ]; user concerns and responses [ ]; worker workload review [ ]; unresolved limitations [ ]; conditions of acceptance [ ]; retest triggers [ ]; responsible reviewer/date [ ]. Do not infer Canada compliance from U.S. ADA dimensions.

docs.title: Fire, hygiene and materials coordination brief
docs.body:
## One assembly, several reviewers
The same change can affect flame behavior, escape, cleaning, moisture and access. Assign facilities as coordination owner and obtain separate decisions from fire/code, hygiene, accessibility and operations reviewers. A supplier's 'commercial grade' description is not an approval.
## Fire and egress inquiry
Identify occupancy, installation location, floor-versus-wall/fixture use, thickness, exposed area, substrate, adhesive and proximity to escape routes or heat sources. Ask the code professional which test/classification and edition applies to this configuration. E648 is a floor-covering critical-radiant-flux method [S11]; other uses may invoke different requirements. Do not reuse one material's floor report as evidence for a noodle-shaped fixture guard or untested adhesive combination.
Record report scope, specimen match, test laboratory, code reference, required class, result, and authority determination. Confirm that trims, barriers and installation staging preserve the applicable escape route. Fire approval does not imply traction or hygiene acceptance.
## Cleaning validation
Before procurement, cleaning staff demonstrate the proposed routine on a mock-up using the actual product, soil, dilution, machine/pad and drying method. Look for residue, tackiness, odor, staining, tearing, slippery film, liquid ingress, inaccessible seams and inability to dry within the operating window. Health/food-safety reviewers set any required microbial or other verification; appearance alone cannot demonstrate sanitation.
## Food zones
The FDA Food Code is a model and the current landing page identifies a 2026 edition [S4]. Determine the locally adopted text and the specific food preparation/storage/customer area requirements. Do not assume an allowance or prohibition from another zone or jurisdiction. Obtain the applicable local public-health determination for Canadian food premises.
## Material and environmental dossier
Request composition restrictions relevant to the market, emissions evidence if applicable, SDS for installation/cleaning chemicals where required, safe curing/ventilation conditions, expected degradation, repair method and disposal instructions. 'Non-toxic,' 'eco-friendly' and 'antimicrobial' require defined evidence and do not establish overall suitability. Do not add antimicrobial claims as a program benefit without relevant support.
## Disposal and continuity
Budget for adhesive removal, substrate restoration, waste segregation and locally applicable disposal. Do not promise recycling without an available accepting facility. Maintain spare stock and a compatible approved temporary control; do not improvise a new untested material during a supply shortage.

docs.title: Evidence register and commissioned research protocol
docs.body:
## Status of the evidence
The pack uses a targeted review of official guidance, standards scopes and a relevant primary trial. It does not establish a pooled child-retail injury reduction, a preferred commercial product or a universal benefit-cost ratio. The distinction is material: a plausible biomechanical effect and a retail clinical benefit are different claims.
## Evidence categories used
VERIFIED SOURCE FACT: a narrow statement supported by the cited source. PROGRAM RECOMMENDATION: our proposed operating rule or engineering approach. ILLUSTRATION: invented inputs used to explain a method. UNRESOLVED: information the site must obtain. These labels are not formal GRADE ratings. Every source must retain its population, setting, product and jurisdiction limits.
## Priority claim ledger
| Claim | Category | Evidence | Decision implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wet/contaminated surfaces require active control | Guidance-based source fact | [S2], [S15] | Address sources and cleaning |
| Access requirements constrain surface selection | Source fact, local scope required | [S1], [S14] | Mandatory accessibility review |
| The FLIP system did not demonstrate benefit in its studied setting | Trial finding | [S8] | Do not claim generic cushioning efficacy |
| F1292 is a playground impact specification | Public standards scope | [S7] | No retail safety certification inference |
| This program reduces child-retail injuries by X% | Unresolved | No estimate established here | Do not publish a percentage claim |
| Commercial guard attachment can fail | Engineering risk to investigate | Product-specific tests needed | Evaluate actual system and aging |
## Reproducible review to commission
Question: in public-facing retail environments involving children, which environmental or operational controls reduce same-level falls, collisions or injury severity without increasing access/worker burdens? Define interventions, comparators, age groups, outcomes and eligible designs before searching. Search health/engineering databases and trial registries plus regulator sources; log exact query, platform, date and coverage. Include adverse and null findings; search references and manufacturer evidence with conflict flags. Have two reviewers independently screen and extract; document exclusions and resolve disagreements.
Extract population, setting, system, comparator, denominators, duration, outcome definitions, effect/interval, confounding, attrition, reporting changes and funding. Separate retail-child evidence from adult-care and laboratory evidence. Assess design-appropriate bias; avoid combining incompatible outcomes. Do not call this proposed review completed until the search and screening records exist.
## Burden-data research
NEISS can inform product-associated emergency-department injury patterns [S19]; CHIRPP offers sentinel injury descriptions with coverage limitations [S20]. Neither supplies store visits or proves a product caused an injury. Predefine narrative coding, duplicate handling and ambiguous-setting rules; obtain method review before weighted estimates. No national retail-child total is invented in this pack.

docs.title: U.S. localization pathway with California example
docs.body:
## National framework, local determination
Use the ADA and relevant worker rules as starting layers, then establish state/local building, fire, public-health, liability and privacy requirements for the actual site. DOJ distinguishes existing-facility barrier removal from new construction and alterations [S14]. Do not infer an existing store is exempt merely because no large renovation is planned.
## Required routing
1. Operator supplies jurisdiction, ownership, occupancy and intended work.
2. Counsel/accessibility professional determines ADA and state obligations.
3. Code professional identifies adopted construction/fire editions, local amendments and alteration classification.
4. Building/fire officials confirm permit/inspection routes within their remit.
5. Health authority reviews food-related zones; safety lead checks the relevant worker-safety regime.
6. Property, insurance and procurement parties finalize contractual permissions and acceptance evidence.
## California illustration — not the selected pilot location
The BSC bulletin states the 2025 California Building Standards Code applies to permit applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026, with the preceding edition applicable to the described earlier applications [S17]. Local amendments, existing-building provisions, work scope and subsequent updates still matter. A new purchase date alone does not establish the governing code.
California Title 8 section 3273 addresses permanent work surfaces, including dangerous projections/obstructions, repair and slippery conditions [S16]. This is worker protection; it is not a complete statement of duties to child customers. Request separate counsel review of customer/premises obligations and preservation/reporting rules.
## Illustrative completed routing row
Topic: walking surface. Type: LAW—applicability pending. Candidate reference: California Title 8 section 3273. Proposed reviewer: employer safety lead. Missing evidence: actual California site and covered work conditions. Decision: UNRESOLVED. This example demonstrates honest recording, not compliance approval.
## No universal product approval
Ask whether a floor or guard is subject to product-specific rules as well as building installation requirements. CPSC carpet/rug flammability guidance [S12] cannot simply be assigned to every resilient material. Classification, warnings, documentation and installation obligations must match the actual product.
## Release criteria
Signed local applicability matrix; permits or documented 'not required' determination; reviewed as-built configuration; required inspections; operator ownership; no critical open conditions. Archive source/version and recheck when scope or regulations change.

docs.title: Canada localization pathway with Ontario example
docs.body:
## National framework, provincial implementation
Use NRC model publications as reference material and establish provincial/territorial adoption and local enforcement. The existence of the 2025 national model codes [S6] does not tell a site which edition governs its work. Confirm the responsible building/fire offices and any local health, worker-safety, accessibility, human-rights and occupiers' liability duties.
## Ontario illustration — not a selected pilot
Ontario's official accessibility page describes the 2024 Building Code's role in new construction and extensive renovations and its relationship to the Design of Public Spaces standard [S18]. This page was available through the official search extract; direct retrieval failed during this review. A local professional must verify the current legal text, amendments, transition provisions and exact project scope before relying on it.
Do not interpret the building-code treatment of existing buildings as eliminating separate accessibility/customer-service or human-rights obligations. Conversely, do not represent every indoor floor change as automatically falling under an outdoor/public-space standard. Record the precise applicable provisions and reasoning.
## Routing worksheet
Province/territory [ ]; municipality [ ]; property/occupancy [ ]; proposed work [ ]; building legislation and edition [ ]; fire requirements [ ]; public-health office [ ]; worker-safety regime [ ]; applicable accessibility/human-rights requirements [ ]; product/material restrictions [ ]; privacy law [ ]; lease responsibilities [ ]; permits and inspections [ ]; professional and authority references [ ].
## Safety and research interfaces
CCOHS same-level fall guidance is useful for operational hazard identification [S15], but it is not the province's statute. An academic research partner should determine the application of TCPS 2 and institutional research ethics rules; a research pilot can require review even if short [S22]. Do not use public visibility of a store as an automatic consent exemption for an intervention study.
## Release criteria and language
Use the same evidence gates as the U.S. framework, with Canadian requirements and units. Provide appropriate language/access formats for the community and applicable obligations. Do not translate U.S. legal labels or inches into a Canadian compliance statement. Record all unresolved points and route them to a named local reviewer before purchasing an installed system.

docs.title: Statistical analysis and feasibility planning appendix
docs.body:
## Pre-analysis plan fields
Protocol/version [ ]; primary estimand [ ]; unit of allocation [ ]; unit of analysis [ ]; sites [ ]; periods [ ]; exposure definition [ ]; event adjudication [ ]; statistical method [ ]; missingness rules [ ]; confounders [ ]; multiplicity approach [ ]; software/reproducibility record [ ]; independent analyst [ ]. Lock the plan before reviewing comparative results; label subsequent analyses exploratory.
## Rates and comparisons
Rate = events / matching exposure × 100,000. Distinguish falls, falls with injury, collision events and injured persons. Repeated events and multiple injuries cannot be mixed casually. Report intervention and comparison counts and exposure with uncertainty. Use appropriate Poisson/negative-binomial or other justified models with exposure offset and site/time structure; check overdispersion and clustering. A before/after difference alone does not remove seasonal or reporting effects.
## Rare-event illustration
Assume, for planning only, a baseline rate of 2 injury events per 100,000 entries. A pilot with 100,000 entries would expect only 2 events if that assumption were true. Zero observed events would be unsurprising enough that strong efficacy claims are inappropriate. Under a simple independent Poisson model with perfect ascertainment, the one-sided 95% upper rate bound with zero events is −ln(0.05)/exposure, approximately 3/exposure. At 100,000 entries this is about 3 per 100,000, not zero. Real clustering, ascertainment and exposure error may invalidate that simple calculation.
## Sample-size commissioning
Specify the minimum effect worth detecting, acceptable error rates, baseline rate uncertainty, cluster size/variation, between-site correlation, exposure forecasts, dropout and loss development. Ask the statistician for scenarios rather than one falsely precise number. If required exposure exceeds available resources, state the study is a feasibility pilot and choose operational outcomes accordingly. Do not fabricate a powered design without these inputs.
## Missing and changing data
Keep unknown age/severity separate; do not assign missing reports to no injury. Define exposure-outage handling before analysis. Audit whether reporting rises after training; interpret near-miss increases alongside safety culture and conditions. Maintain a versioned correction log and reproducible aggregate analysis dataset.
## Decision interpretation
Report confidence intervals, potential biases and external validity, not only statistical significance. Lack of statistical significance is not proof of equivalence or no harm. A significant package effect does not isolate foam's contribution. Report all pre-specified balancing outcomes and explain deviations. Decide scale, redesign, extension or removal using document 25.

## Meeting agenda template

## Escalation and dependency control

docs.title: Funding, incentives and commercial adoption pathways
docs.body:
## Separate existing mechanisms from new proposals
Existing conditional U.S. mechanisms: IRS guidance describes the Disabled Access Credit for eligible small businesses and an architectural barrier-removal deduction [S23]. These apply to qualifying expenditures under their rules, not automatically to foam, general child-safety improvements or participation in this program. Obtain current-year tax advice and documentation before assuming any benefit. No tax amount is included automatically in the calculator.
Proposed mechanisms: municipal/provincial/state pilot grants, shared testing vouchers, philanthropic injury-prevention funding, group procurement and insurer incentives. No available award, open application window or insurer commitment is established here. Canadian funding must be researched for the actual applicant and location rather than asserted nationwide.
## Funding stack worksheet
Source [ ]; existing/proposed [ ]; administering body [ ]; applicant eligibility [ ]; eligible expense [ ]; amount/cap [ ]; match [ ]; deadline [ ]; award/approval evidence [ ]; restrictions [ ]; duplicate-funding rule [ ]; reporting [ ]; owner [ ]. Count only confirmed awards in a committed budget; show speculative sources separately.
## Pitch structure by funder
Business sponsor: capped learning investment, maintained legal controls and explicit removal reserve. Public funder: shared evidence, equitable access, small-business feasibility and transparent procurement. Foundation: defined prevention question and independent evaluation. Insurer: measurable risk controls and loss/exposure data. Manufacturer: testing/service contribution with independence and publication protections; support does not buy favorable conclusions.
## Small-business route
Offer an assessment-first option emphasizing repairs, layout and operating procedures before capital flooring. Pool independent technical advice or purchasing only after each site establishes fit. Standardize paperwork and training, not assumptions about identical hazards. Provide budget for staff participation, accessible advisory input and removal.
## Procurement and competition
Use performance criteria and allow equivalent approaches. Declare conflicts, retain rejected-bid reasons and do not use a sponsor's product as the mandatory standard. A shared testing program should define ownership/access to results and treatment of system variants.
## Decision memo
Confirmed financing [ ]; unconfirmed opportunities [ ]; minimum viable safe scope [ ]; maintenance funding [ ]; removal funding [ ]; downside affordability [ ]; approval conditions [ ]. If safe maintenance cannot be funded, reduce or defer the candidate installation while continuing ordinary hazard correction.

docs.title: Coalition governance and independent assurance charter
docs.body:
## Proposed structure
Create a steering group chaired by the operator/sponsor, with facilities, frontline workers, accessibility/disability representatives, community caregivers, insurer/risk advisors and independent evaluation expertise. Invite authorities within their remit without implying endorsement. Suppliers contribute technical information but do not adjudicate their own evidence.
## Decisions and accountability
Operator retains responsibility for safe premises and work. The steering group coordinates, budgets and reviews the program; it cannot waive law or shift duties to unpaid advisors. Professional reviewers sign only within competence. Authorities retain statutory powers. Public participation is advisory unless a specific governance agreement assigns otherwise.
## Charter fields
Purpose [ ]; members/roles [ ]; chair/deputy [ ]; terms [ ]; meeting frequency [ ]; quorum [ ]; decision method [ ]; conflict policy [ ]; independent review rights [ ]; budget authority [ ]; records custodian [ ]; public-report policy [ ]; complaint route [ ]; renewal/closure [ ]. Suggested quorum: sponsor/operator, operations, relevant technical reviewer and evaluation lead, with accessibility input for access decisions. Adopt locally; this is not a statutory requirement.
## Independence controls
Declare financial and professional interests at appointment and when an agenda item changes. Recuse conflicted members from supplier award and independent outcome judgment. Contracts should preserve access to necessary data and the right to report adverse/neutral findings within agreed privacy and confidentiality limits. Do not allow a funder to rewrite scientific conclusions.
## Assurance plan
First line: staff inspections and manager follow-up. Second line: corporate risk/facilities review of records and configuration. Third line: independent technical/evaluation audits at defined milestones. These are proposed assurance layers, scaled to program size. Independence must be documented, not inferred from a job title.
## Complaints and escalation
Offer accessible channels, acknowledge complaints within a locally adopted target, triage urgent hazards immediately, and report resolution without exposing personal details. Record complaints about accessibility, cleaning, worker burden and communications as safety information. Allow dissent in decision records. Escalate unresolved critical conditions to sponsor and relevant authority as required.
## Program identity
Use 'participating pilot site' only when participation is real and current. Do not issue 'certified child-safe' badges. A future certification scheme would need separate standards, independent conformity assessment, surveillance, appeals, misuse controls and governance; none is created by this kit.

docs.title: Ready-to-adapt procurement statement of work
docs.body:
## 1. Invitation and objective
[Buyer] invites proposals to address [hazard IDs] at [site/zone] under the Child-Safer Spaces program. Bids may propose repair, redesign, operational improvement or a purpose-designed protective assembly. Selection is based on demonstrated suitability and whole-life cost; no particular foam or brand is required.
## 2. Scope and site information
Provide site access for assessment at [time]. Buyer supplies [plan, exposure, loads, substrate facts, cleaning methods, known constraints]. Bidder must verify conditions relevant to its design and list assumptions. Scope includes design coordination, applicable submissions, mock-up/testing, installation, commissioning, training, maintenance instructions, traceability and removal/restoration planning. Exclusions must be explicit.
## 3. Required submission
Technical approach and alternatives; exact system/configuration; compliance and approval assumptions; independent evidence and limits; completed acceptance schedule; risk/failure analysis; work and closure plan; accessibility/cleaning/load compatibility; qualifications; warranty/remedies; itemized pricing; recurring/replacement/removal costs; lead times; conflicts; references for comparable uses. Supply reports, not just marketing summaries.
## 4. Evaluation and clarification
Mandatory criteria in document 08 are pass/fail. Unresolved mandatory evidence prevents award for public installation. Weighted scoring applies only to eligible submissions using document 09. Buyer may request clarification or independent testing; changes are documented and provided fairly to bidders. Do not convert a lowest-price decision into a claim of safety equivalence.
## 5. Deliverables and hold points
D1 survey and design; D2 accepted test/approval plan; D3 mock-up and dossier; D4 installation records; D5 commissioning and required inspections; D6 training and handover; D7 scheduled follow-up; D8 defects/removal support. No concealed work or public reopening past a hold point without the designated written release.
## 6. Commercial schedule for legal completion
Contract price/currency [ ]; taxes/freight [ ]; milestones and retainage [ ]; insurance [ ]; permits [ ]; defects response [ ]; warranty [ ]; change control [ ]; recall/product-change notices [ ]; ownership of reports [ ]; confidentiality/privacy [ ]; indemnity/liability [ ]; termination/restoration [ ]; dispute/governing law [ ]. Local counsel must complete and align with the actual contract.
## 7. Acceptance
Acceptance requires evidence against every applicable criterion, resolved critical defects and signed operator/technical releases. Payment, use of the space or a vendor certificate must not be treated as a substitute for the agreed acceptance process. Preserve statutory rights and duties as determined by counsel.

docs.title: Audit, corrective action and effectiveness verification
docs.body:
## Audit scope
Audit whether the actual installed system, people and procedures match the approved program. Sampling cannot prove the absence of all hazards. Audit high-risk zones and adverse findings deliberately; do not sample only the easiest sites. Proposed cadence: commissioning, first month, formal pilot review, and after material changes or serious concerns, supplemented by risk-based independent reviews.
## Audit checklist
| Area | Evidence to inspect | Failure requiring action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Configuration | As-built, lot IDs, approved substitutions | Unreviewed material/adhesive change |
| Routes | Actual layout during busy/restocking periods | Obstruction or new access/escape barrier |
| Maintenance | Logs, observed work, chemical compatibility | Missing inspections, incompatible treatment |
| Product condition | Seams, movement, guards, ingress | Detachment, instability, contamination |
| Training | Demonstration and shift coverage | Staff cannot perform critical response |
| Data | Event/exposure windows, duplicates, missingness | Invalid rates or understated missing data |
| Claims | Notices, presentations and partner references | Unsupported efficacy or certification claim |
| Governance | Open actions and signed releases | Gate treated as complete without evidence |
## Finding classification — program definitions
Critical: immediate serious safety/access/egress concern or an unaccepted system creating plausible harm; isolate and escalate. Major: required process/evidence absent or systematic failure; assign prompt containment and sponsor review. Minor: bounded documentation/process defect without a known critical condition; correct by assigned date. Review facts rather than relying on labels to delay protection.
## Corrective action form
Finding ID [ ]; site/zone [ ]; condition/evidence [ ]; classification [ ]; containment [ ]; root-cause analysis [ ]; correction [ ]; systemic prevention [ ]; owner [ ]; due date [ ]; retest/verification method [ ]; verifier independent of correction where feasible [ ]; result [ ]; recurrence review date [ ].
## Effectiveness check
Verify the cause is addressed, not merely that a task was marked done. Example: after replacing a curling mat, check whether saturation, cart movement or fit caused recurrence. Sample subsequent operating periods and cleaning cycles. Reopen the finding if the defect returns. Link recurring product issues across sites/batches.
## Audit report
Scope and sample [ ]; limitations [ ]; findings [ ]; overdue actions [ ]; unresolved critical conditions [ ]; management response [ ]; independent reviewer [ ]; next review [ ]. Do not average critical failures into an overall passing percentage.

docs.title: Worked fictional example and completed sample records
docs.body:
## Illustration only
Example site EX-001 is a fictional family-oriented general retailer. No real company, product, incident history, price or approval is represented. These examples are stored separately from blank live registers so they cannot be mistaken for actual site evidence.
## Assumed observations
At the entrance, a mat moves after loaded carts cross it and rainwater tracks around its edge. At one queue fixture, an exposed corner is contacted by passing carts. The rest of the aisle floor appears intact during this limited walk; that does not establish full-site safety.
## Proposed response
Isolate the unstable area under the existing procedure and establish a safe route. Investigate entrance water management and mat fit/securement. Ask facilities to assess relocating or replacing the queue fixture with rounded geometry. Do not begin by covering the store in foam. If a commercial guard is still proposed, review attachment, projection, cleaning and fire requirements before procurement.
## Sample records
| Record | Example entry | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H-EX-01 | Entrance mat movement after cart crossing; immediate control: isolate and notify | Observable condition and action |
| A-EX-01 | Facilities to investigate source and replacement system; status open | Owner and pending work, not invented completion |
| R-EX-01 | Fire/code applicability for new guard: unresolved; reviewer needed | Honest jurisdiction gate |
| T-EX-01 | Wet/loaded mock-up criteria: not set; specialist approval pending | No post hoc pass threshold |
| G-EX-03 | Product suitability remains blocked | A plan is not a test report |
## Illustrative rate calculation
Assume 3 reported injury falls in 150,000 baseline entries and 2 in 120,000 follow-up entries. Rates are 2.0 and 1.67 per 100,000 entries. Raw counts and the apparent rate change do not establish benefit: counts are small, exposure/reporting may differ and no valid comparator is specified. Record uncertainty and proceed with the analysis plan rather than advertise a reduction.
## Illustrative financial result
Use document 17's hypothetical 15,000 initial cost and sensitivity cases to understand the calculator. They are not quotes for this fictional site. If costs, tests or maintenance are unaffordable, narrow the capital pilot and continue ordinary hazard correction. A no-go decision on a product can be a successful evidence-based outcome.

docs.body:
## Send only after local review
These drafts are unsent. Replace placeholders and use authorized organizational channels. Do not name a partner, claim endorsement or imply an approved installation unless documented. Sequence outreach to resolve actual decisions: sponsor → facilities/property/accessibility → authorities → insurer → suppliers → community/evaluation partners.

We request a capped assessment and feasibility pilot for [site] addressing [hazard mechanisms]. The program compares repair, design and operational controls with commercially engineered protective options. We are reviewing walking routes and fixture hazards at [site] and invite adult advisors to help identify practical access issues. Participation is voluntary; accessible formats and [compensation arrangements] are available. We will explain the proposed activity, privacy handling and any ethics review before participation. Advisors are not asked to certify safety, attempt dangerous tasks or provide children's personal information.

We seek an independent partner to refine a feasibility protocol and determine the evidence needed for an effectiveness study. Please propose outcome definitions, exposure measurement, comparison design, sample-size scenarios, ethics/privacy pathway, analysis and publication arrangements. Disclose relevant commercial relationships. Null and adverse findings must be reportable under agreed privacy protections.
## Supplier clarification request
Please identify the exact assembly your report represents and any differences from our proposed substrate, adhesive, finish, thickness or use. Provide relevant wet/aged/loaded/cleaned results and limitations. Explain what would require retesting. Marketing claims or playground-only evidence cannot substitute for the acceptance schedule.
## Follow-up and meeting close
Thank you for reviewing [specific question]. Our outstanding items are [ ]. Please identify the responsible decision-maker, required evidence and expected review steps. We will record the matter as unresolved until a written determination is received. Meeting close: decisions [ ]; advice versus binding conditions [ ]; actions/owners/dates [ ]; next review [ ].
## Public-facing start
Use document 23's factual notice once the site's details and contacts are confirmed. Report changes people can actually see and use. Never recruit support by exaggerating injury burden or blaming caregivers for environmental hazards.

docs.title: Ethics determination and data-sharing agreement outline
docs.body:
## Research versus operations
Routine hazard correction proceeds through existing safety processes. A planned intervention study, structured participant testing or secondary data research requires an applicable ethics/privacy determination before that research activity begins. U.S. OHRP explains that intent to publish alone does not decide whether an activity is research [S21]. Canada's TCPS 2 distinguishes non-research quality activities from research and includes research pilots within review scope where the policy applies [S22]. These sources do not grant an exemption for this project.
## Determination request
Institution/site [ ]; sponsor/funding [ ]; purpose and research questions [ ]; activities [ ]; participants/age groups [ ]; intervention [ ]; identifiable information [ ]; recruitment/consent [ ]; risks and mitigation [ ]; data linkage [ ]; intended dissemination [ ]; applicable institutional policies [ ]. Obtain the authorized office's written determination and conditions; keep its reference in G1/G3 as appropriate.
## Participant protection
Use adults for initial usability discovery. Separate consent from access to ordinary services or employment expectations. Explain withdrawal, recording and compensation. Avoid collecting personal injury stories in public feedback. Research involving children needs separate expertise, parental permission/assent arrangements and safeguarding review as applicable; this pack does not authorize it.
## Data-sharing schedule for legal review
Parties and roles [ ]; purpose [ ]; permitted dataset/fields [ ]; prohibited re-identification [ ]; legal basis/consent [ ]; security/access [ ]; transfer method and location [ ]; retention/deletion [ ]; onward sharing [ ]; breach notification [ ]; audit rights [ ]; publication and small-cell review [ ]; intellectual property [ ]; termination [ ]; signatories [ ]. No raw claims or CCTV transfer is presumed.
## Minimum analytical dataset
Prefer site-period aggregate counts, exposure, intervention dates and operational measures. If coded event-level data is necessary, justify each field and separation of keys; coded data can remain identifiable in context. Keep time/location granularity only as needed and assess linkage risks. Do not treat removing names as sufficient anonymization.
## Release gate
Privacy officer and evaluation lead confirm that analysis/publication matches the approved purpose, disclosures and data controls. Keep negative results; protect identities. An organizational confidentiality review must not become an undisclosed mechanism for suppressing unfavorable findings.

docs.title: Year-by-year economics and scenario interpretation
docs.body:
## Extended model
The workspace now supports constant annual operating costs and retained-loss assumptions, annual escalation, a scheduled replacement and terminal salvage. It shows each year's cash flow, discounting and cumulative recovery. All inputs are user assumptions. No actuarial loss development, tax calculation or validated efficacy estimate is embedded.
## Inputs and conventions
Initial cost includes design, approvals, testing, materials, installation, closure, training and reserve. Year-1 retained addressable loss means the business's expected costs for mechanisms this intervention could affect, net of costs borne by others. Reduction may be negative to model worsening losses. Other savings must be independently supported and non-overlapping. Annual escalation applies consistently to loss, other savings and operating cost starting in year 2. Replacement is a one-time nominal amount at the selected year-end; salvage is a year-end amount only at the horizon. Discount rate and cash flows must be consistently nominal or real.
## Calculation
Annual gross benefit at year t = (year-1 retained loss × assumed reduction + year-1 other savings) × (1 + escalation)^(t−1). Net cash flow subtracts escalated operating cost and scheduled replacement, adding terminal salvage. Present value divides by (1 + discount)^t. NPV includes negative initial cost at time zero. First cumulative recovery is reported, but a later replacement can reverse recovery; inspect the whole table. This model uses no residual value for the reserve unless entered as salvage, a conservative convention that must be reviewed.
## Scenarios
Run worsening, no-effect, modest-benefit and favorable-benefit cases without treating any as a forecast. Evaluate shorter life, more cleaning labor, closure cost, recurring replacement and lower retained loss. A discounted break-even reduction tells you the effect needed under the assumptions; it does not indicate that effect is achievable or likely. If greater than 100%, the stated economics cannot break even solely through the modeled loss reduction.
## Cost of evidence and equity
Include independent review, advisory compensation, accessible materials and staff time. These are real costs even if no injury improvement is detected. A sponsor can choose to fund learning or accessibility outcomes without claiming financial payback; state that objective explicitly. Separate societal benefits from business cash flows rather than adding them invisibly to ROI.
## Review and export
Finance validates quotations, currency, timing and allocation. Risk/actuarial staff validate retained-loss inputs and loss development. The evaluation lead owns the uncertainty in reduction. Export the scenario and year table with assumptions so another reviewer can reproduce it.

Document exact verification achieved and any limits in VERIFICATION.md.
## Content acceptance criteria
No invented partner, insurer concession, code approval or product efficacy. Every legal/standards statement retains scope. Illustrative examples remain separate from live records. Critical unresolved requirements block readiness. Public statements distinguish participation, feasibility and effectiveness. Templates name owners, evidence and the decision they support.
## Unfinished real-world work
Select site and team; verify local requirements; collect baseline/exposure; engage advisors; obtain supplier/independent reports; approve thresholds; secure funding and permissions; install and commission if authorized; train staff; run/evaluate pilot; make and sign scale decision. This list describes implementation dependencies, not missing fictional documents to be filled with guessed facts.

docs.title: Entity playbooks and first deliverables
docs.body:
## Business sponsor
Start with 02, 03, 10 and 17. Decide the assessment scope and budget; name operator and deputies; fund review and rollback. First deliverable: signed charter plus budget envelope. Do not instruct procurement to buy a material before suitability review.
## Store manager and workers
Start with 12–14, 28, 36 and 47. Walk hazards, assign response coverage, maintain safe routes and log defects. First deliverable: current hazard/action list and shift procedure. Escalate critical conditions immediately; ordinary safety work does not wait for a research protocol.
## Facilities, accessibility and fire/code reviewers
Start with 06–08 and 29–31. Define the actual assembly and work scope; identify applicable rules and measurable acceptance criteria. First deliverable: coordinated requirements/test schedule with unresolved conditions. Review dimensions and operations at the actual installation, not only drawings.
## Insurer, broker or self-insured risk team
Start with 19, 15–17 and 44. Clarify coverage/notice requirements and addressable retained losses; specify evidence needed for any later risk recognition. First deliverable: written review questions and policy-specific conditions. No premium reduction is presumed.
## Government/public-health staff
Start with 07, 20, 33 or 34. Identify remit and routing, review proposals through ordinary processes and consider evidence-support options. First deliverable: local requirements/authority response or policy-review pathway. Participation in discussion is not endorsement.
## Suppliers, laboratories and installers
Start with 08, 09, 21, 29 and 39. Submit exact configuration evidence, limitations, itemized cost and maintenance/removal terms. First deliverable: completed dossier and acceptance schedule; list all untested assumptions.
## Landlord and contractors
Start with 22, 11, 12 and 31. Resolve alteration permission, leak/substrate ownership, shift handovers, compatible cleaning and reinstatement. First deliverable: agreed responsibility schedule incorporated into actual contracts.
## Community advisors and researchers
Start with 24, 30, 32, 35 and 43. Identify practical access concerns and evidence questions, agree participation safeguards and preserve independent findings. First deliverable: feedback themes or evaluation proposal with limitations. Do not ask advisors to certify safety.
## Everyone
Use the task board for non-sensitive coordination, the gate tracker for evidence references and the document library for role-specific packs. Keep official signatures, personal records and confidential contracts in approved systems. Review G0–G6 together at handovers.

docs.title: Operational job aids and scenario exercises
docs.body:
## Opening checklist — adopt and localize
Confirm designated responders/deputies; walk entrance/aisle/queue routes; inspect mats, seams and guards; verify supplies and barriers; check open defects/closures; verify safe accessible and escape routes; review weather/restocking/cleaning plans; record time, findings and owner. Reopening a previously closed area needs its release, not just an opening checklist tick.
## Handover checklist
Outgoing lead communicates open hazards, isolated zones, temporary routes, incomplete cleanup, repair visits, product changes and missed checks. Incoming lead acknowledges ownership and records the next required action. Do not leave 'contractor will handle it' without a named responsible role and confirmation.
## Scenario A: wet entrance with curled mat
Expected response: protect customers and workers; maintain safe access/egress; notify lead; address water and unstable mat under the approved procedure; verify before reopening; log response and source investigation. Wrong inference: more padding automatically fixes the hazard. Debrief: who owns saturation and replacement checks?
## Scenario B: guard partly detached after cleaning
Expected response: isolate contact area as needed, prevent access to loose parts, preserve product/batch evidence and notify facilities. Do not push it back or use an unapproved adhesive. Review cleaning compatibility and attachment; inspect matching installations. Restart only after approved correction and verification.
## Scenario C: customer reports wheelchair difficulty
Expected response: offer assistance through the site's accessible service process, record the barrier without unnecessary personal data, and escalate the affected route for review. Do not dismiss the complaint because a lab report passed. Stop use of a system that creates an unresolved access barrier.
## Scenario D: zero injuries in month one
Expected response: report counts and exposure honestly, inspect data completeness and balancing measures, and continue the planned review. Do not display a claim that the floor prevents injuries. Ask whether reporting changed and whether exposure is sufficient for inference.
## Knowledge check and answer key
Can a warning sign alone isolate a hazard? No; use the site control procedure. Does playground testing approve a retail aisle? No. Who sets test thresholds? The competent reviewer before testing. Who can stop use? Staff initiate hazard isolation under the procedure; assigned leaders manage formal closure/restart. Where do medical/claims details go? The protected organizational system.
## Competency release
Learner role/code [ ]; exercise [ ]; critical steps demonstrated [ ]; missed steps/retraining [ ]; trainer [ ]; date [ ]; supervisor verification [ ]. Review whether staff have time, equipment and authority to carry out the process; training cannot compensate for an impossible workload.

docs.title: Launch dossier and go/no-go review agenda
docs.body:
## What may launch today
The planning program: name owners, approve assessment resources, inspect and correct hazards through existing procedures, organize records and request specialist/authority/supplier input. This launch does not authorize an unreviewed physical installation or intervention study.
## Physical pilot launch dossier
Index the signed charter; site/zone plan; local applicability and permits; landlord agreement; exact accepted assembly; independent reports and mock-up; approved installation and commissioning records; training/shift coverage; cleaning/maintenance plan; removal reserve and method; privacy/ethics determination; evaluation protocol; incident contacts; public notice; and all open conditions.
## Go/no-go meeting agenda
1. Confirm scope and actual configuration, including substitutions.
2. Review each mandatory criterion and required authority determination.
3. Demonstrate operating readiness and safe alternative route.
4. Review all adverse findings, dissent and unresolved questions.
5. Confirm data quality, evaluation limits and honest public claims.
6. Confirm budget, maintenance capacity and removal ability.
7. Record a decision: go under stated conditions, revise/retest, defer, or reject/remove.
## Non-negotiable no-go conditions — program rules
Unresolved critical safety/access/fire/health condition; required permission missing; unknown performance of the offered system against a mandatory criterion; unavailable competent operator/maintenance coverage; inability to restore a safe surface; or a research activity lacking the required determination. A sponsor's enthusiasm or supplier warranty cannot waive these conditions.
## Decision form
Site [ ]; scope/version [ ]; meeting date [ ]; attendees by role [ ]; evidence index [ ]; conditions [ ]; no-go items [ ]; decision and rationale [ ]; dissent [ ]; authorized signatories [ ]; launch date if approved [ ]; first inspection/review [ ]; expiry/review trigger [ ]. Formal signatures belong in the controlled record, not a browser checkbox.
## After launch
Publish only the approved factual notice, inspect early operating/cleaning cycles, maintain response capacity and review all concerns. Report material adverse findings promptly through the defined channels. Changes reopen affected gates. At pilot end, decide scale, extend, redesign or remove using document 25 and retain the evidence for future sites.
